place.zh: 沉鼎观 · 柴房 · 开春

setup.zh: 正月里，家里的回信到了。开了春，周衡那一篮残株送到了。
setup.en: In the first month the letter from home came. In spring, Zhou Heng's basket of culls arrives.

recap.zh: 开春的残株一株一株喂进饭桶，开出三颗九转聚气丹；分堆一认，认出三张方子——打那夜起，照方子喂，进步神速；灵石先见了底。阿禾、孙二狗的书案底下，各多了一个油纸包。
recap.en: The spring culls went into the Rice Tub one by one and gave three nine-turn qi pills; sorted into heaps, they gave up three recipes — from that night he fed by recipe and advanced by leaps, and the spirit stones ran out first. Under A-He's desk and Sun Ergou's, an oilpaper packet each.

en: The letter from home: the roof is mended.
A basket of culls, thrown out.

story.zh: 正月里，家里的回信到了。坊市逢十九有集，蒙山来的信客在钱掌柜的摊子边上支一张小桌，收信，交信；他的家信，走的都是这张小桌。他娘的字小，写得密：屋顶修了；五两银子腊月里送到了，你爹便再没往黑松岭那头去过。末了一句是：吴婆婆让我捎一句话给你，她说：「告诉那孩子，牙还在。」我问她什么牙，她不说，只是笑。
story.en: In the first month the reply from home arrived. The market held a fair on every nineteenth, and the letter-carrier from Mengshan set up a little table beside Shopkeeper Qian's stall, taking letters and handing them out; every letter from home came over that little table. His mother's hand was small and close: the roof was mended; the five taels had come in the twelfth month, and your father has not gone out toward Black Pine Ridge since. The last line was: Granny Wu asked me to pass you a message. She said: "Tell the boy, the tooth is still there." I asked her what tooth; she wouldn't say, only smiled.

exits.means: feeds the spring culls into the Rice Tub: three nine-turn qi pills, two given away; sorts the basket by herb and finds the three recipes (黄精+灵石 → 聚气丹, 黄芪+a breath → 回春丹, 紫玉参+a breath → 回气丹) in a few lines — 进步神速, and 灵石 run out before 黄精

story.zh:
好容易熬到开了春，药园开了园，周衡那一篮残株便送到了。这是小满巡夜的工钱：黄精的烂根，黄芪的虫叶，当归的歪苗，篮底还压着两根紫玉参的断须。他嚼一株，喂它一株，开出来的多半是灰和烟；半个月喂下去半篮，开出三颗[聚气丹]{注=qi-pill}，青白透亮，九道纹——外门份例里每月一颗的，是一道纹的。

他爹说，打猎靠的不是运气，是脚印。他把剩下的半篮按样分成四堆，蹲着把这半个月的脚印一个一个往回认，认了一夜，认出三张方子：黄精搭一块灵石，出聚气丹；黄芪搭一口自己的气，出回春丹；紫玉参的断须搭一口气，出回气丹，丹田空了吞一颗，一口气灌回来大半缸。乱搭的，仍旧是灰。方子他一个字也没往纸上写，记在肚里。

打这以后，饭桶吐一颗，他吃一颗；吃一颗，涨一截。开春还是四层，不出一个月便过了五层。说书的在这里省一句话：靠这饭桶的丹药，沈小满进步神速。只有一样不省事：黄精月月有，灵石月月见底——份例三块，喂一回便没了。他站在执事堂那面墙底下，看那些写着「灵石」的牌子，头一回觉得那不是牌子，是丹。

过了两日，讲堂上阿禾和孙二狗的书案底下，各多了一个油纸包，包里一颗聚气丹。小满只说是利息：孙二狗那一颗，是牛棚里那半张饼的；阿禾那一颗，他没说。旁人问起来路，小满便说是秘境里捡的：潭边一个死人，袋子里有一只瓶。

阿禾把那颗丹对着窗户的光转了一圈，嘴唇一动一动的，是在数纹。数到第九道，她的嘴唇停住了。她什么也没问，原样包好，揣进怀里，没有吃。

孙二狗却当夜就吃了。天亮的时候，孙二狗从练气零层，冲到了一层。他站在大通铺门口，把一只手摊在太阳底下，瞧着掌心里那一缕细细的黄气，瞧得眼泪鼻涕一齐流了下来。褚先生说过，伪灵根引气，五年起步；他进山门还不满一年。

这一哭，哭坏了事。一个零层的伪灵根，一夜引了气，不到晌午便传遍了外门，天黑前传进了内门；传来传去，只剩一句：沈小满手里有丹，好丹。
story.en:
At last spring came; the herb garden opened, and Zhou Heng's basket of culls arrived. It was Xiaoman's pay for the night watch: rotten Solomon's-seal roots, worm-eaten astragalus leaves, crooked angelica seedlings, and at the bottom two broken root-hairs of purple jade ginseng. He chewed one, fed it one; what came out was mostly ash and smoke. Half a month took half the basket and gave three qi pills, clear as pale jade, nine rings — the ones in the outer court's monthly allowance had one.

His father used to say hunting runs on tracks, not luck. He sorted the rest of the basket into four heaps by kind and squatted there reading the half-month's tracks back one by one; a night of it, and he had three recipes. Solomon's seal with a spirit stone gave a qi pill; astragalus with one breath of his own qi gave a mending pill; a purple jade ginseng root-hair with one breath gave a qi-restoring pill — dantian run dry, swallow one, and most of the jar came back in a single breath. Anything mixed was still ash. He never put a word of the recipes on paper; he kept them in his head.

From then on the Rice Tub gave a pill and he ate it; a pill eaten, a stretch gained. Layer four at the start of spring, and within the month he was past five. The storyteller will spare you a sentence here: on the Rice Tub's pills, Shen Xiaoman advanced by leaps and bounds. Only one thing was not spared him: Solomon's seal came every month, and spirit stones ran out every month — three in the allowance, and they went in a single feeding. He stood under that wall in the Hall of Errands, looking at the tags that said *spirit stones*, and for the first time saw not tags but pills.

Two days later, under A-He's desk and Sun Ergou's in the lecture hall, there was an oilpaper packet each, a qi pill inside. Xiaoman said only that it was interest: Sun Ergou's on half a flatbread in the cowshed; A-He's, he didn't say. When others asked where they came from, Xiaoman said he had picked them up in the secret realm: a dead man by the pool, a bottle in his bag.

A-He turned the pill once in the light from the window, her lips moving — counting rings. At the ninth her lips stopped. She asked nothing, wrapped it up as it was, tucked it into her jacket, and did not eat it.

Sun Ergou ate his that very night. At daybreak, Sun Ergou broke from Qi Condensation layer zero to layer one. He stood at the dormitory door with one hand held open in the sun, looking at the thin yellow wisp of qi in his palm, until tears and snot ran down together. Master Chu had said a false root takes five years at the least to draw in qi; he had not been a year inside the gate.

That crying spoiled everything. A false-root boy at layer zero drawing in qi in a single night — before noon the whole outer court knew it, and by dark the inner court too; passed from mouth to mouth, only one sentence was left: Shen Xiaoman has pills, good ones.
